1.title: Quick-Reference Recap and Service Chooser
1.text: Welcome to Module fifteen: Quick-Reference Recap and Service Chooser. There is no new task statement here. This module puts the whole course on a few pages: look-alike services side by side, need-to-service choosers, and the lists and terms to remember. Use it for your last review before the exam.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do four things. See the whole exam on one page. Tell look-alike services apart, in pairs and sets. Use need-to-service choosers for questions that describe a requirement. And recall the lists the exam likes, and the terms that trip people up.

1.title: Case Check-In: Lantern and Loom's Final Review
1.text: Lantern and Loom's platform is now secure, resilient, fast and lean. Before the exam, you want one page per topic, not fourteen modules. Some look-alikes keep getting mixed up: S Q S and S N S, peering and Transit Gateway, and Multi-A Z and read replicas. Your job is to review quickly, and fix the confusions that cost points.

1.title: The Exam on One Page
1.text: Here is the exam on one page. Secure Architectures is thirty percent, in modules one to three: I A M, service control policies, K M S, W A F, Shield, encryption and compliance. Resilient Architectures is twenty-six percent, in modules four and five: decoupling, Multi-A Z and disaster recovery strategies. High-Performing Architectures is twenty-four percent, in modules six to ten: storage, compute, databases, network and edge, and ingestion. Cost-Optimized Architectures is twenty percent, in modules eleven to fourteen. There are sixty-five questions, fifty scored and fifteen unscored, in one hundred thirty minutes, with seven hundred twenty to pass. Exam tip: security carries the most weight, yet cost is still one question in five.

1.title: Look-Alikes: Security and Identity
1.text: First, security and identity. An I A M user has long-term keys; a role gives temporary credentials that are assumed; Identity Center gives workforce single sign-on. A service control policy is an account guardrail and never grants access; a permissions boundary caps one identity; an identity policy grants access. K M S manages keys; CloudHSM is a dedicated hardware module; A C M handles T L S certificates; Secrets Manager rotates secrets. W A F applies web rules; Shield handles D D o S; GuardDuty detects threats; Inspector scans for vulnerabilities; Macie finds sensitive data in S three. CloudTrail shows who called the A P I; Config shows configuration history; CloudWatch holds metrics and logs. And security groups are stateful at the instance, while network A C L s are stateless at the subnet. Exam tip: say the one-line job of each service.

1.title: Look-Alikes: Decoupling and Integration
1.text: Next, decoupling and integration. S Q S is a queue, pulled by one consumer; S N S fans out by push; Event Bridge is an event bus with rules. A standard queue is at-least-once with best-effort order; a Fifo queue is ordered, with no duplicates. Kinesis Data Streams has ordered shards and custom consumers; Firehose delivers to S three and more; M S K is managed Kafka. Step Functions orchestrates steps, while S Q S buffers messages. The Application Load Balancer works at layer seven, the Network Load Balancer at layer four with static I P addresses, and the Gateway Load Balancer fronts inline appliances. A P I Gateway is the managed A P I front door, and Amazon M Q runs Active M Q and Rabbit M Q for migrated applications. Exam tip: loose coupling means a queue, topic or event bus between the parts.

1.title: Look-Alikes: Resilience and Recovery
1.text: Now resilience and recovery. Multi-A Z gives high availability with a standby; a read replica scales reads; Multi-Region is for disaster recovery. The four strategies are backup and restore, pilot light, warm standby and active-active; recovery time falls from hours to seconds, and cost rises each step. R P O is the data you can lose; R T O is the time to recover. Route fifty-three failover switches on health checks, latency routing picks the fastest Region, and weighted routing splits traffic. Aurora Global Database gives cross-Region relational replicas, and DynamoDB global tables give multi-Region tables. A W S Backup is policy-based backup, and Elastic Disaster Recovery replicates servers continuously. Exam tip: match the R T O and R P O to the cheapest strategy that meets them.

1.title: Look-Alikes: Storage and Databases
1.text: Now storage and databases. S three is object storage; E B S is block storage for one instance; E F S is shared Linux files; F S x covers Windows, Lustre, Net App O N T A P and Open Z F S. R D S runs managed engines; Aurora is cloud-native, with six copies across three zones and up to fifteen replicas. DynamoDB is key-value; Dax is a microsecond cache for DynamoDB; ElastiCache is an in-memory cache for others. Redshift is a warehouse; Athena runs S Q L on S three and charges per query. Timestream holds time series, Keyspaces is Cassandra, Document D B is Mongo D B-compatible, and Neptune is a graph database. For moving data, DataSync is online bulk, Transfer Family is S F T P, Storage Gateway is a hybrid cache, and Snow is offline. Exam tip: pick the data model first, then the service.

1.title: Look-Alikes: Compute, Network and Edge
1.text: Now compute, network and edge. E C two gives servers; Lambda gives functions, up to fifteen minutes; Fargate runs containers without servers. E C S is A W S-native orchestration; E K S is Kubernetes. CloudFront caches H T T P content; Global Accelerator gives static anycast I P addresses for T C P and U D P. Peering connects two V P C s; Transit Gateway is a hub for many; Private Link shares one service privately. Direct Connect is a dedicated private link; Site-to-Site V P N is encrypted over the internet. A gateway endpoint covers S three and DynamoDB at no charge; an interface endpoint uses Private Link, billed hourly plus per gigabyte. Exam tip: static I P addresses and no caching mean Global Accelerator; cache it means CloudFront.

1.title: Look-Alikes: Ingestion and Analytics
1.text: Finally, ingestion and analytics. Glue is serverless E T L with a catalog; E M R runs Hadoop and Spark clusters; Athena runs S Q L on S three. Lake Formation manages permissions and governance for a data lake. QuickSight builds dashboards, and OpenSearch handles search and log analytics. AppFlow moves software-as-a-service data, and the Database Migration Service migrates and replicates databases. Kinesis streams data in, M S K is Kafka, and Firehose delivers it. Parquet and O R C are columnar formats; C S V and Jay-son are row formats. Exam tip: query it where it sits with Athena; move and clean it with Glue; visualize it with QuickSight.

1.title: Service Chooser: Secure and Resilient
1.text: Here is the first chooser. Temporary access for an app to S three: an I A M role. Encrypt with keys you control and audit: a K M S customer managed key. Block web exploits: W A F; absorb D D o S: Shield. Limit what member accounts can do: a service control policy in Organizations. Survive an Availability Zone failure: Multi-A Z plus Auto Scaling. Survive a Region loss: cross-Region replication plus Route fifty-three failover. And buffer a traffic spike: S Q S. Exam tip: name the verb in the need, such as encrypt, block, buffer or fail over, then the service.

1.title: Service Chooser: High-Performing and Cost-Optimized
1.text: Here is the second chooser. Cache static content worldwide: CloudFront. Fixed I P addresses with fast failover: Global Accelerator. Low-latency key-value at scale: DynamoDB, with Dax. Shared Windows files: F S x for Windows File Server. Steady baseline compute: Savings Plans, with restartable work on Spot. Unknown S three access: Intelligent-Tiering; rare access: Glacier, by lifecycle. And private servers reading S three: a gateway endpoint. Exam tip: cost clues are steady, unknown, rare, restartable and idle.

1.title: Lists and Terms the Exam Likes
1.text: Lists are easy points. The Well-Architected pillars are operational excellence, security, reliability, performance efficiency, cost optimization and sustainability. Disaster recovery strategies, cheapest first, are backup and restore, pilot light, warm standby and active-active. S three classes, hot to cold, are Standard, Intelligent-Tiering, Standard-I A, One Zone-I A, Glacier Instant, Glacier Flexible and Glacier Deep Archive. The purchase options are On-Demand, Savings Plans, Reserved Instances and Spot. Know R P O and R T O, horizontal and vertical scaling, stateless and stateful, and eventual and strong consistency. Exam tip: say each list aloud from memory.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. One page: four domains, sixty-five questions, one hundred thirty minutes, and seven hundred twenty to pass. Look-alikes: learn the one-line job of each service, because the exam describes the job. Choosers: name the verb in the need, then the service. Lists: pillars, disaster recovery strategies, S three classes and purchase options. And terms: R P O, R T O, horizontal, vertical, stateless and eventual consistency. In Module sixteen, we cover exam technique.
